newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end up but more weakness forecast.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end up but more weakness forecast.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled higher on steady speculative buying, but market sources remained wary of pegging today's session as the beginning of an uptrend.
"I think the market will take a breath and then resume the downtrend," an analyst said.
Most-active March settled 0.60 higher at 80.40, traded 81.00 to 79.25. Spot January ended up 0.80 at 76.40. The deferred months finished 1.50 lower to 0.60 higher.
Support remained at 68.50 on the ten-year chart, and then at 65.45, a low made in Feb 1993. Nearby resistance was pegged at the bottom of a former downtrend channel at 81.80 in March.

PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko noted that despite a technically oversold condition based on the Relative Strength Index and the stochastics readings, the market has failed to stage an impressive rally.
"Perhaps traders aren't as bearish as we've been lead to believe," Savaiko said, noting a reading this week of 44 percent on the Bullish Consensus survey of market sentiment.
A reading of 25 percent bullish or lower indicates an oversold condition, he said.
Open interest also remains high, in contrast to prior major market bottoms in which open interest fell sharply due to speculative long liquidation, he said.
